last.verdict: Berkshire is finally shrinking its share count, buying back $9.6 billion, but weaker car insurance pulled core profit down about 6%.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock, more than double the prior quarter and about $14.4 billion year to date. Reuters says roughly $2 billion more was bought in early October.

takeaways.label: Core profit slips
takeaways.text: Operating earnings fell to $12.7 billion from $13.5 billion a year earlier. Railroad, utilities and manufacturing grew, but lower insurance and investment income outweighed them.

takeaways.label: GEICO margins shrinking
takeaways.text: Insurance underwriting profit fell to $1.35 billion from $2.37 billion. GEICO's pre-tax profit nearly halved to $982 million as injury claims and expenses rose and it charged lower premiums to win back customers.

takeaways.label: Stock buying stalls
takeaways.text: Berkshire was a slight net seller of stocks, about $0.4 billion, after heavy net buying last quarter. Cash also funded the $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison purchase, with reported cash still above $350 billion.

history.verdict: Berkshire's profit slipped as car-insurance earnings fell, but it more than doubled share buybacks to about $9.6 billion.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock in the quarter, more than double the prior quarter's $4.5 billion, and about $14.4 billion so far this year.

takeaways.label: Insurance profit drops
takeaways.text: After-tax underwriting profit fell 43% to $1.35 billion. GEICO's pre-tax profit nearly halved to $982 million as injury claims got costlier and expenses rose 17%.

takeaways.label: Core earnings dip
takeaways.text: Operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7 billion. Rail, utilities and manufacturing grew, but lower interest income and weaker insurance more than offset them.

takeaways.label: Stock buying stalls
takeaways.text: Berkshire sold slightly more stock than it bought, a net $0.4 billion, after a net $19.8 billion of purchases last quarter. Cash was also used on the $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison deal.

history.verdict: Investors cheered Berkshire finally spending its cash pile on buybacks and stocks.

reasons.label: Big share buybacks
reasons.text: Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the quarter, up from small buybacks before.

reasons.label: Cash put to work
reasons.text: Berkshire became a net stock buyer for the first time in about 14 quarters, with a Alphabet stake included.

reasons.label: Stronger operating profit
reasons.text: Operating earnings rose about 16% to $13.0 billion, though insurance underwriting profit slipped to $1.7 billion.
